title: FESCO Bill Calculator 2026 (Latest Tariff) | Wattlyst
meta: Estimate your FESCO bill from units with the 2026 NEPRA slabs, fixed charge, QTA, GST and the latest NEPRA FPA. How sanctioned load changes it.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: What is the FESCO per unit rate?
p: FESCO bills the uniform A-1 domestic tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026; it sets none of the rates itself. An unprotected home in Faisalabad, Sargodha, Jhang, Mianwali, Khushab, Bhakkar, Toba Tek Singh or Chiniot pays the rate of the slab its monthly units reach on every unit: 350 units are all billed at Rs 36.46. Protected consumers pay two low rates slab by slab, and lifeline consumers less again.

What this page adds to the per unit rate is the fixed charge, which many FESCO consumers overlook. It is charged per kW of sanctioned load, and the rate per kW rises with the slab the month reaches, so the table below is built around sanctioned load rather than units alone.

sections.h2: How does the sanctioned load change a FESCO bill?
p: Two homes using the same 350 units can get different bills because of the kW printed in their connection details. On 2 kW the fixed charge is Rs 800 and the bill comes to Rs 18,401; on 4 kW the fixed charge is Rs 1,600 and the bill Rs 19,345. The fixed charge is also inside the GST base, so the gap grows a little further after tax.

A sanctioned load of 5 kW or more moves the connection to the time-of-use tariff with peak and off-peak rates and a fixed charge on the higher of half the sanctioned load or the recorded maximum demand, which this calculator does not model. If the bill was raised after a load extension for an AC or a motor, check the kW it now prints.

sections.h2: FESCO summer vs winter bills in Faisalabad
p: Faisalabad summers are long and hot, and the AC decides the bill from May to September. A one and a half ton inverter split draws up to about 1,450 W, so a few hundred units a month is normal with one unit running through the night. In the examples, a summer month of 550 units on 3 kW costs Rs 32,262, while a winter month of 150 protected units costs Rs 3,395.

Because the summer months break the protected run, the lower rates come back only after 6 bills in a row under 200 units. The AC units calculator estimates the units for your tonnage and hours; enter the result here to see the FESCO bill.

sections.h2: FESCO bill check: the printed lines and the reference number
p: This FESCO bill estimate works from the figures you type and does not fetch your account. On the printed bill, take the units from the difference between the two meter readings, the sanctioned load from the connection details, the category from the tariff line and the FPA from its own line. The official bill, with the reference number, due date and arrears, is on the FESCO website, which links the duplicate bill on the PITC portal; enter the reference number from the top of an earlier bill there.

If the reading dates on the bill cover more than a month, the units may have crossed a slab because of the long cycle; the bill audit tool checks that. Every bill also carries an FPA line; see what the FPA line on your bill means. A home on a time-of-use meter can check the peak hours for FESCO.
Faisalabad, Sargodha, Mianwali, Khushab, Jhang, Bhakkar, Toba Tek Singh and Chiniot, from its head office in Faisalabad. If your bill carries another company's name, use that company's calculator.

faq.q: How do I get a FESCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and the sanctioned load from the bill, tick protected only if the bill prints that category, and replace the pre-filled FPA with the one on your bill under advanced settings. For 350 units on 2 kW the estimate is Rs 18,401, FPA included.

faq.q: What is the FESCO per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The uniform NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab the month reaches: Rs 36.46 per unit for an unprotected home using 350 units. Protected and lifeline consumers pay less, and the fixed charge per kW is added on top.

faq.q: Is the FESCO tariff different from LESCO or MEPCO?
faq.a: No. The 2026 tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026 is uniform for all ex-WAPDA DISCOs and K-Electric. NEPRA sets one FPA for every DISCO too, so a FESCO bill for the same units and sanctioned load equals a LESCO bill; real bills differ only by billing days, arrears and local items.

faq.q: What is the fixed charge on a FESCO bill?
faq.a: A monthly charge per kW of sanctioned load, at a rate that depends on the slab the month reaches. For 350 units on 2 kW it is Rs 800; the table above shows how it grows with each extra kW.

FESCO serves eight districts: Faisalabad, Sargodha, Mianwali, Khushab, Jhang, Bhakkar, Toba Tek Singh and Chiniot. Faults and billing complaints go to the national electricity helpline 118 (call, or SMS 8118).

faq.q: How do I check my FESCO bill online?
faq.a: The FESCO website links a duplicate bill page on the PITC portal; enter the reference number printed at the top of an earlier bill to see the current bill and due date. This calculator estimates the bill from units; it does not fetch your account.

faq.q: Why does my FESCO bill differ from this estimate?
faq.a: The estimate uses the pre-filled FPA unless you enter your bill's, and it cannot see arrears, late payment surcharge or meter rent. Check that the sanctioned kW you entered matches the bill, and if the reading dates cover more than a month, run the bill audit tool.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: A bill of Rs 25,000 or more a month carries advance income tax under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001: 7.5% of the bill for a domestic consumer who is not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List. This calculator leaves it out because it depends on your tax status; check the income tax line on your bill and FBR's current withholding tax card.

key_facts: FESCO, the Faisalabad Electric Supply Company, supplies Faisalabad, Sargodha, Mianwali, Khushab, Jhang, Bhakkar, Toba Tek Singh and Chiniot from its head office in Faisalabad and bills the uniform NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff for 2026, not a tariff of its own.
An unprotected FESCO consumer using 350 units pays Rs 36.46 on every unit, which is Rs 12,761 of energy charge before the fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA and GST.
The fixed charge is per kW of sanctioned load at the rate of the slab reached: 350 units on 2 kW carry a fixed charge of Rs 800, and the same units on 4 kW carry Rs 1,600, before GST.
A FESCO protected consumer is one whose last 6 bills were all at or under 200 units on a connection below 5 kW; a Faisalabad summer month with an AC usually ends that run.
GST at 18% is charged on the energy charge, fixed charge and surcharges together and adds Rs 2,807 to a 350 unit FESCO bill; the surcharge and GST defaults are secondary-source figures that change.

The bill jumps at 700 units: up to there every unit is billed at Rs 41.85, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of Rs 47.20, which adds Rs 4,480 to the bill of an unprotected 2 kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Looking for a FESCO tariff of its own. FESCO bills the uniform NEPRA domestic slabs; only the monthly FPA is specific to the month.
Entering one kW when the bill prints more. After a load extension for an AC or a motor the fixed charge is per kW of the new sanctioned load, every month.
Ticking protected after the first summer month. One bill over 200 units moves the home to unprotected rates for the next 6 months.
Using this calculator for a connection of 5 kW or more. Those are billed on ToU peak and off-peak rates with a different fixed charge.

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for July 2026 charged on September 2026 bills. October 2026 bills carry Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, reported in the news; this page keeps the latest NEPRA-verified rate until that decision is published. Replace it with the FPA rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit). Protected homes pay it too; lifeline bills carry none.

content.answer: A FESCO home in Faisalabad using 350 units in a month as an unprotected consumer on a 2 kW connection pays about Rs 18,401: Rs 12,761 energy charge at Rs 36.46 per unit, Rs 800 fixed charge for the sanctioned load, plus FC surcharge, QTA, the July 2026 FPA and GST. FESCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges, then GST.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC, QTA, FPA = per-unit surcharges printed on the FESCO bill
